summary: Twelve comment-endorsed tools, services, games, museums, articles, and learning resources from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 12 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Audacity 4.0
items.summary: A major update to the open-source audio editor for recording and destructive editing.
items.why_included: A returning user called the new release a massive improvement and praised its low-friction voice recording.
items.evidence: The commenter uses Audacity for voice clips because it is less hassle than their main audio tool.

evidence_sources.author: ch_fr
evidence_sources.excerpt: I have used old audacity and musescore-owned audacity, and I have to say it's a massive glow-up.

items.name: Forward Email
items.summary: A privacy-focused email forwarding and hosted-mail service for custom domains.
items.why_included: A custom-domain owner uses it for family addresses and praised its privacy policy.
items.evidence: The commenter uses Forward Email for family mail addresses and considers its privacy policy reasonable.

evidence_sources.author: decimalenough
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use forwardemail.net and they have a pretty reasonable privacy policy:

items.name: Cerebras Inference
items.source_story_title: Qwen 3.8 27B available on Cerebras at 1500 tokens/s
items.summary: A cloud inference service optimized for unusually fast large-language-model responses.
items.why_included: A first-hand coding test found the speed premium worthwhile for a short session.
items.evidence: The test completed a code-review session quickly, though it cost $1.60 and briefly hit rate limits.

evidence_sources.author: eli
evidence_sources.excerpt: The Cerebras session cost me $1.60 and took a total of 5.1 mins. I did get a few brief 429 rate limit errors in there.

items.name: Thousand Year Old Vampire
items.source_story_title: Any Human Ever – One life, drawn at random from all who have ever lived
items.summary: A solo journaling role-playing game about memory, loss, and an immortal life.
items.why_included: A commenter called it terrific and suggested pairing it with historical-life generation.
items.evidence: The commenter positively recommended the game for story-driven play.

evidence_sources.author: pavel_lishin
evidence_sources.excerpt: Thousand Year Old Vampire, a pretty terrific journaling game:

items.name: Unusual Suspects
items.summary: A browser drawing game that compares your suspect sketch with the revealed person.
items.why_included: A player loved the reveal and found the sketch comparison hilarious.
items.evidence: The commenter played the game and praised its funny reveal mechanic.

evidence_sources.author: neverkn0wsb357
evidence_sources.excerpt: This game is hilarious. I love the reveal, how my poor, horribly drawn, mobile touch-based drawing compares to the actual person; the juxtaposition was really funny.

items.name: The National Museum of Computing
items.source_story_title: The Computer Museum of America reclamation project
items.summary: A Bletchley Park museum with working computers, mainframes, Bombe replicas, and Colossus.
items.why_included: A recent visitor called it fantastic and highlighted its playable working systems.
items.evidence: The visitor praised the museum's broad collection of operational machines.

evidence_sources.author: plapsley
evidence_sources.excerpt: It was fantastic. They have a wide variety of working systems that you can play with, from home computers to mainframes, as well as Bombes and the Colossus (used to break the Lorenz cipher), and WITCH.

items.name: HomeComputerMuseum
items.source_story_title: The Computer Museum of America reclamation project
items.summary: A Dutch hands-on computer museum where visitors can use the collection.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended it as a great experience for children and adults.
items.evidence: The commenter praised its large, usable collection and broad family appeal.

evidence_sources.author: decide1000
evidence_sources.excerpt: The computers can be used by anyone. Really a great experience for kids these days and adults.

items.name: Holden's Lightning Flight account
items.summary: The accidental pilot's own account of taking off in an English Electric Lightning.
items.why_included: A commenter specifically recommended reading Holden's first-person account instead of a retelling.
items.evidence: The commenter directed readers to the primary account beginning on page three.

evidence_sources.author: js2
evidence_sources.excerpt: I would say it's worth reading Holden's account of it directly, which starts on page 3 of this PDF:

items.name: Xanadu: The Internet That Might Have Been
items.summary: Gwern's critical history of Project Xanadu and its unrealized hypertext design.
items.why_included: A commenter called it a compelling counterargument to the usual sympathetic Xanadu narrative.
items.evidence: The commenter endorsed Gwern's argument that Xanadu's omitted features were fundamentally unstable or unnecessary.

evidence_sources.author: ameliaquining
evidence_sources.excerpt: In my view, Gwern makes a compelling counterargument: Xanadu was a fundamentally bad idea.

items.name: What I learned from my mom (1941-2026)
items.source_story_title: What I learned from my mom (1941-2026)
items.summary: A personal tribute distilling lessons from the author's late mother's life.
items.why_included: A reader called it a favorite and praised both the article and its subject.
items.evidence: The commenter strongly endorsed the tribute as one of their favorite recent reads.

evidence_sources.author: pelcg
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is a great article and this woman is an inspiration to many. Likely one of my favourite reads here.

items.name: ARC Prize
items.summary: An open benchmark and competition tracking progress on abstract reasoning tasks.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended its multi-generation score history as an impressive progress record.
items.evidence: The commenter encouraged readers to explore ARC Prize and praised its score history.

evidence_sources.author: jrflo
evidence_sources.excerpt: You should read more on the ARC prize, it actually has a pretty long history.

items.name: Robot Dexterity Still Seems Hard
items.summary: An analysis of why dexterous physical automation remains commercially difficult.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly included it among recent robotics resources they found useful.
items.evidence: The commenter recommended the article as a useful related read with a similar conclusion.
